title: Boxplots, violin plots and distribution charts

videos.script: Five regions, four hundred deliveries. Are some regions slower than others? {{question}} Five histograms side by side would answer it, but they are hard to compare. Each has its own shape, its own bars, its own height. {{histograms}} A boxplot squeezes each distribution into five numbers. The lowest and the highest. The two quartiles, which hold the middle half between them. And the median. {{five}} Draw five of them next to each other and the comparison takes a second. Centre-West and Northeast are a little slower. The South is a little faster. And the boxes overlap so much that the differences between regions are smaller than the differences inside each one. {{compare}} But five numbers are a summary, and a summary can hide. Two groups can have identical boxes and completely different data. {{hide}} This lesson teaches you to read a boxplot, to see what it hides, and to show the points or the shape when they matter. {{plan}}
